# Master Category Architecture v1.0 (build v1.99.104)

Implements the structure recommended in the Elecmetric vs Omni Calculator comparison. **Nothing public changes**: no page, URL, sitemap entry or visitor-facing file was edited. This is the registry the site can be generated from later.

## Files (all generated by `node tools/build_master_architecture.js`)
| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `docs/Elecmetric_Master_Category_Architecture_v1.0.csv` | 20 Level 1 categories (with long-term targets and reserved capacity), 129 Level 2 subcategories, 128 Level 3 topics that hold tools today |
| `docs/Elecmetric_Master_Tool_Mapping_v1.0.csv` | All 304 existing tools (246 engine, 58 standalone): Level 1/2/3, tool type, legacy category and subcategory, verification |
| `docs/COUNT_RECONCILIATION.md` | What each published count (246, 300/305, 304, 649, 669) actually counts |
| `tools/master_architecture.json` | Machine-readable version for future page generators |
| `tools/master_architecture_ids.json` | Tool IDs given to standalone pages (EM-00247 onward); stable, never renumbered |

`tests/master_architecture_test.js` (in CI) fails when a tool is unclassified, an ID repeats, or the generated files are stale.

## Design decisions
- Subject (Level 1/2/3) and tool type are separate. Tool types are the nine from the strategy: Calculator, Converter, Generator, Solver, Estimator, Analyzer, Simulator, Reference, Worked Example. Reference and Worked Example have no tools yet; they describe the 294 formula and converter pages, which are not in the tool count.
- Level 1 targets are the strategy's long-term portfolio (3,020), not a launch requirement. Level 2 is not split into targets because that would be invented numbers.
- Existing Elecmetric categories (C01-C24) map to Level 1 and 2. Legacy IDs stay in the CSV so the older register and All Tools keep working.
- No tool is Verified. Verification stays separate from category.

## For your decision (editorial judgement, easy to change in the mappings at the top of the generator)
1. **Electrical-unit converters** (kW to amps, kVA to kW, HP to kW and 12 more) are placed in Unit Conversion & Measurement > Electrical Units, as the strategy's section 5 says. Their legacy category was Power or Cable.
2. **Statistics and probability tools** moved to Statistics & Data Analysis (6 tools); everything else from the old Engineering Mathematics group is in Mathematics.
3. **Binary, hex, BCD, Gray, ASCII and Unicode tools** stay in Engineering > Electronics Engineering (Digital Electronics), as the register already had them. Computer Science & IT is empty.
4. **Lighting** sits under Electrical Engineering (the strategy's list has no lighting topic; one was added). Alternative: Physics > Optics.
5. **Data centres, railway and building MEP** are placed in Electrical Engineering, Rail Electrification (under Automotive & Transportation, added) and Electrical Engineering. Rail has one tool.
6. **Solar and wind** are in Energy & Environment; **batteries** stay in Electrical Engineering (the strategy lists Batteries in both).
7. **Airport and Aviation Engineering** is a Level 2 under Engineering and is flagged "Featured hub" in the mapping, as recommended.

## Not done, by design
- No homepage, hub, URL, sitemap or All Tools change. The strategy says to introduce categories only once each has enough real tools; today only Engineering (207 tools) and Mathematics (63) pass any reasonable threshold.
- No new calculators or categories were published. The five coming-soon hubs from v1.99.103 are unchanged.
- No independent engineering review process was created; that needs named reviewers.

## Suggested next steps
1. Review the seven decisions above.
2. Fix the public count wording (see COUNT_RECONCILIATION.md).
3. Add a Tool type filter to All Tools using the nine types, then Level 1 filters.
4. Add Level 1/2 breadcrumbs to calculator pages from this registry.

## Update: All Tools filters (done)
All Tools (`/calculators/all-tools/`) now has a **Subject area** filter (Level 1) and the "Browse Tools by Calculation Type" chips use the nine strategy tool types (Calculator, Converter, Solver, Estimator, Analyzer, Simulator, Generator, Reference). Counts update with the other filters, as before. Data comes from `tools/master_architecture.json`; the build stops if a catalogue item has no Level 1 or tool type. Converter and formula pages take the Level 1 of their old category and are typed Converter or Reference. URLs, sitemap and indexable pages are unchanged. Still open: Level 1 landing pages, breadcrumbs, new categories and the named-reviewer process.
